slides.title: Two Indias, one week
bullets: Khalid Jamil's senior squad is in New Zealand
Naushad Moosa leads a mostly U-23 side in Dhaka
The defending champions are still perfect
slides.question: Should India keep sending its young side to SAFF?

concept: A split-screen idea told in type instead of pictures: the hero slide sets the senior team in muted grey and the back-up side in bright white, so the eye lands on the team nobody expected to be the story. Slide 2 turns the whole match into one number, the 38th minute, because a single penalty decided it. Slide 3 names the 'two Indias' and hands the debate to the audience. Football green tag, no photos or logos.
caption:
India's B-team just did the job.

With Khalid Jamil's senior squad away for friendlies in New Zealand, a mostly U-23 India side under Naushad Moosa beat Maldives 1-0 in Dhaka to top Group B at the SAFF Championship.

Suhail Bhat's 38th-minute penalty (his third goal of the tournament) settled it, and keeper Priyansh Dubey's late saves kept the clean sheet. Two wins from two, six points, and the defending champions are into the semi-finals on November 14, where Prothom Alo reports they will face Bhutan.

Is sending the young side to SAFF smart squad-building, or should India always field its best XI? Tell us below.
